artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan unifying the batch session-id across session-register/acquire-retry/release in research.md, plan.md, implement.md; correcting the inline rationalization prose; threading the bare batch id into implement.md's per-task skill dispatch to fix the Stage 4D dual-heartbeat gap; reconciling task-lock.md's contradictory same-session-bypass passage; and extending test-conflict-predicate.sh Group 9 with sibling static guards.

memory_candidates.content: Lock/registry session ids and per-task bookkeeping session ids are two different things in this agent system, and conflating them is a live defect class. Any value passed to task-lock.sh session-register / acquire / acquire-retry / release / heartbeat / session-heartbeat for one batch MUST be one byte-identical bare session id, because session_contention()'s self-exclusion (in scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh) is an exact string match on session_id: a per-task-suffixed variant makes the batch's own union-file_scope registration read as a foreign live session and refuses every acquire in the batch against itself. Per-task-suffixed ids remain correct for NON-lock purposes (skill_preflight_update bookkeeping, the Agent context id surfaced in .return-meta.json, commit trailers). When a downstream agent fires two heartbeats (task-lock heartbeat + session-heartbeat) from one context session_id, both can only succeed if the dispatching caller threads the bare batch id into the dispatch args -- fix that at the caller that owns the value, not in the agent. Note also that instruction-document prose can actively rationalize such a defect as intentional; the prose must be corrected in the same phase as the call site, or it re-teaches the bug.
